protocol.description:
A private protocol between eave (the status bar) and hypr-eave (its Hyprland plugin). The client draws its islands opaque, in their own fill color, exactly as it would without the plugin. It tells the compositor which parts of each frame are islands that may turn to glass, and in which fill color, and the compositor lets the frosted, refracted backdrop through where a pixel is that fill color. In return the compositor tells the client how bright it is behind its surface, so the ink of islands over something bright can turn dark and stay readable.
Since version 2 it also says where the notch and the grown edge are, in every theme, so the compositor can draw the pointer under them, the way a physical notch hides it. A client without glass sends only those.
Since version 3 the client can also say how high the glass floats over what's behind it (set_gap).
Since version 4 it can say where its controls are cut into the glass or stand out of it, so the glass bends at their walls too (set_reliefs).
Since version 5 it can say where its pictures are, rounded, so the glass shows through their rounded corners and they're kept as drawn inside them (set_pictures). Before it, pictures are solid records.
When the global is absent the client draws as it would anyway: nothing depends on it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created through it are not affected.

entry.name: already_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has an eave_glass_surface_v1

request.name: get_glass
request.description: Raises already_exists if the surface already has one.

interface.name: eave_glass_surface_v1
interface.description:
All requests set double-buffered state, applied on the surface's next wl_surface.commit, so what they say lands with the frame it describes. Coordinates are surface-local, in logical pixels.
Once the wl_surface is destroyed the object is inert.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The glass goes on the surface's next commit.

entry.name: glass
entry.summary: an island: its fill color turns to glass

entry.name: solid
entry.summary: content that never lets glass through, over any island

entry.name: bezel
entry.summary: the notch or the grown edge: solid, and the pointer goes under it

request.name: set_regions
request.description:
An array of records, each seven native-endian 32-bit integers: x, y, width, height (signed), kind (see the kind enum), fill (an ARGB color, the island's exact fill) and ink (0 to 255: which way the island's grey ink goes over the glass, 0 lighter, 255 darker, and in between while it turns). Fill and ink are ignored for solid and bezel.
A glass record is the island's shape as the client drew it. A pixel belongs to the nearest one, if it's close: an island's pixels may reach a little past the shape while it moves. It may turn to glass only where it's that island's fill color, and not inside a solid record: the rest of the island, its text, icons and other content, is kept. Pixels near no glass record are never touched.
A bezel record is the notch or the grown edge, exactly where it's drawn. The compositor draws the pointer under the surface there, so the surface's opaque pixels cover it and its clear ones let it through; elsewhere the pointer stays on top. It doesn't keep glass out: a solid record does that.
The initial value is empty: no glass. At most 64 records: the compositor ignores the rest. 64 also keeps the request well inside one Wayland message (4096 bytes).

request.name: set_look
request.description: Lengths are logical pixels. The initial value is the compositor's defaults.

arg.name: band
arg.summary: how far in from the edge the glass's bevel curves down

arg.name: thickness
arg.summary: how thick the glass is: the backdrop bends through it

arg.name: chroma
arg.summary: spread between red and blue, a fraction of the bend

arg.name: rim
arg.summary: brightness of the edge's reflection and its lit side

arg.name: frost
arg.summary: spread of each blur step, 0 for clear glass

arg.name: depth
arg.summary: how many times the blur halves the backdrop, 1 to 6

arg.name: tint
arg.summary: how much the glass takes the color behind it, 0 to 1

arg.name: ink
arg.summary: what grey ink over glass looks like

arg.name: contrast
arg.summary: with ink readable: the contrast ratio it reaches

arg.name: ink_blur
arg.summary: how wide an area the ink's color is chosen over

request.name: set_gap
request.description: Logical pixels between the glass's underside and what's behind it, 0 to 128. A ray bent at the edge keeps drifting across the gap, so the wider it is, the more of what's behind the edge turns over, as through a glass ball. set_look leaves it as it is. The initial value is the compositor's default.

entry.name: invert
entry.summary: the opposite of the glass behind

entry.name: readable
entry.summary: the opposite of the glass behind, as light or dark as it takes to reach contrast

request.name: set_report
request.description: 0 stops them. Otherwise backdrop events come with cells of this many logical pixels. The initial value is 0.

request.name: set_reliefs

description.summary: what is cut into the glass, or stands out of it

request.name: set_pictures

description.summary: the pictures on the islands, and their shape

request.description:
An array of records, each six native-endian 32-bit integers. Lengths and positions are 24.8 fixed point, in surface-local logical pixels:
x, y, width, height and radius: a rounded rectangle with circular corners, where the client drew a picture over an island's fill; opacity: 0 to 255, how opaque it drew the picture.
Where a picture covers a pixel fully, the pixel is kept as drawn, as in a solid record, however dark it is. Where it covers it partly (its rounded corners' edge, or a faded picture), the pixel is the picture laid over the glass by how much of it the picture covers: the client drew it over the fill by as much. Outside the rounded rectangle, the fill turns to glass as anywhere on the island.
A picture outside every glass record is ignored. The initial value is empty. At most 32 records, the largest first: the compositor ignores the rest.

event.name: backdrop

description.summary: how bright it is behind the surface

event.description: A grid of cells, cell logical pixels square, from the surface's top left, row by row. The cells are as small as set_report asked, or bigger: doubled until the event fits in one Wayland message (4096 bytes), which a client can't receive past. One byte each: how bright the frosted backdrop is there (the luma of its encoded color), 0 to 255. Sent when the average under a glass record moves noticeably, at most about ten times a second, and once more after it settles. An empty grid (no cells) means there's nothing to report any more.

event.name: active

description.summary: whether glass is drawn for this surface

event.description: Sent once on creation and whenever it changes. While inactive (turned off, or on an output the compositor can't draw glass on) islands should draw as they would without glass.
